title: Assembly Errors
body:
### Assembly time 
* Syntax

### Link time
* unresolved external references
* Calling a function with the wrong name

### Run-time behavioral error
* Logic errors

### Run-time fault
* crashes 
* abnormal ends ("abends")
* #### Bus errors ~ (2 bombs)
	* Trying to access memory outside of the 4M of addressable memory.
	* Trying to access access address that doesn't exist or is protected by O/S. 
* #### Address errors ~ (3 bombs)
	* attempted to access word or longword at odd address.
	* usually caused by stray pointer / bad global data setup.
* #### Illegal Instruction ~ (4 bombs)
	* Attempted to execute invalid instruction.
	* usually caused by random jump or execution of data.
* #### Privilege Violation ~ (8 bombs)
	* Attempted execution of supervisor-only instruction from user mode.





The hardware side of the run-time faults is in [[Error Detection]]. Address errors are
usually a missing `even` [[Directives|directive]] after byte data; illegal instructions are
usually a corrupted return address, see [[Subroutines]]. Privilege violations are user code
trying to skip the [[System Call]] doorway into the [[Kernel]].

Same compile / link / run-time split as [[Compile Errors]], [[Logic Errors]], and
[[Runtime Errors]] in [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER SCIENCE 2]], and the same thing
[[Unit testing]] exists to catch in [[INTRODUCTION TO SOFTWARE ENGINEERING]].
